CROSS-REFERENCE OF ABF (IACR ePrint 2026/680, "Open problems in list decoding and correlated agreement", Arnon-Boneh-Fenzi) AGAINST THE 23 OPEN TARGETS.

SOURCES AND ACCESS
- Primary: the hash-pinned rev-2 PDF (title page July 2, 2026; 54 pp), sha256 426a979c13cc61db0f2cdb909067ef4c9f24438859fe0a7a337d2b19b07fcaa5, recovered from `git show 3e6330cf:experimental/data/certificates/abf26.pdf` in /home/u2470931/smooth-read-solomin/rs-mca. accessed=yes (via the supplied deep-read digest; v3 of 2026-07-06 still unfetchable, accessed=no).
- Satellite abstracts I fetched directly this session: ePrint 2026/782 (Krachun-Kazanin-Haboeck, "Failure of proximity gaps close to capacity", rec. 2026-04-20, rev. 2026-04-24) accessed=yes (abstract only; full text accessed=no); ePrint 2026/1432 (Sunghyeon Jo, "Reed-Solomon Mutual Correlated Agreement Beyond the Johnson Radius", rec. 2026-07-13) accessed=yes (abstract only).
- Local target statements read: /home/u2470931/smooth-read-solomin/prize/critical/nodes/{rate_half_band_closure,rate_half_list_adjacent_crossing,integer_code_distance_cert,generator_economy,dli_wcl_slot_1_5_emptiness}/statement.md.

WHAT I RE-DERIVED (this is the load-bearing part of the cross-reference; arithmetic run under prize/tools/ramguard).
ABF's only new list-side engine is Appendix C ("Concrete restatements of [KKH26]"): with L smooth, n = m*s, psi(x)=x^m onto G with |G|=s, the received word x^{rm} is matched by codewords built from r-subsets S of G whose tail u_S has degree <= (r-q-1)m, where q = number of elementary symmetric functions pinned across the family (q=0 in Cor. C.6, q=1 in Cor. C.7 via antipodal common sum 0). Agreement is exactly rm; radius is exactly 1 - r/s.
(a) QUANTIZATION LEMMA. At official rate-1/2 rows n = 2^s' and k = rho*n are powers of two, and m = n/s is a power of two, so the degree window forces sigma := a - k in {0} (C.6) or {0, m} (C.7). Reachable "extra agreement" is therefore 0 or a power of two only.
(b) BAND MISS. At the prize-max razor row (n = 2^41, k = 2^40) the rate-1/2 band is sigma in (2^33, sigma* = 8,592,912,738], i.e. delta in [0.49609240, 0.49609375). It contains no power of two, so ABF/KKH reach nothing in its interior. Their strongest razor-row instantiation is s = 256, r = 129, m = 2^33, sigma = 2^33 (the already-covered endpoint), giving |Lambda| >= binom(127,64) = 2^123.17, which exceeds B* = floor(q/2^128) only for q < 2^251.17 - void at the prize cap.
(c) TABLE 5 REPRODUCED. Their headline concrete attack (delta* = 0.492, soundness >= 2^-125.14) reconstructs exactly as s = 128, r = 65 (odd branch), m = 2^14, sigma = 2^14 at KoalaBear q = p^6 = 2^185.93: binom(63,32) = 2^59.67 > B* = 2^57.93, list/q = 2^-126.26 (they report 2^-125.14 in the t=131 column). The mechanism is confirmed; the result is q ~ 2^186-specific and does not survive to q near 2^256.
(d) TARGET-1 IMPOSSIBILITY (new, and useful). At agreement 3n/4 with k = n/2 the window forces r = 3s/4 and q >= s/4 = |G \ S|; but Prod_S(Y) * Prod_{G\S}(Y) = Y^s - 1, so pinning e_1..e_{s/4}(S) determines Prod_{G\S} outright and every admissible useful family is a SINGLETON. The KKH/ABF engine therefore provably cannot produce 2 codewords, let alone 4 > B* = 3, at agreement 3n/4; it also cannot address agreement 3n/4 - 1 at all (its agreements are multiples of m). The boundary escape (zero-sum r-subsets when (r-1)m = k) is empty at s = 4 because no 3-subset of mu_4 has zero sum. Target 1 is untouched, and now provably not borrowable.

TARGETS WITH RELATION NONE (explicitly checked, no mapping emitted): 3 xr_highcore_collision_count, 6 f3_h3_dsp8_correlation_bound, 8 l1_mixed_petal_amplification, 12 dli_c1r3_gated_envelope_bound. ABF contains no slope/strip geometry, no Kloosterman/autocorrelation inequality, no image-fiber or petal counting, and no raw-ledger envelope material.

SCOOP POSITION
- Headliner A (cyclic quotient-rotation list floor at rate 1/2, c = 2^33) is the one with real published overlap: Cor. C.6/C.7 are unconditional worst-case list lower bounds at rate-1/2 smooth rows, credited to [KKH26] = ePrint 2026/782 (April 2026) and slightly generalized by ABF (July 2026). Ours is strictly stronger at the razor row (reaches non-power-of-two sigma_0 = 8,594,128,895 > sigma*, holds to q = 2^256 with 75-bit margin, covers constant common-support arities); theirs stops at sigma = 2^33 and dies above q = 2^251.17. ACTION: prior-art citation in any writeup, plus an explicit "strict improvement" paragraph. Not a kill.
- Headliners B, C, D, E, F, G: no overlap found in ABF rev 2 or in the satellite abstracts. One open check I could not close: headliner B (Proth q = 1705*2^120+1, B* = 6 but |List| >= 7). Cor. C.6 gives >= binom(s,r) codewords at agreement rm for free at every smooth row; if B's exhibit sits at an agreement of the form rm with (r-1)m < k <= rm, it is a special case of a July-2026 published unconditional bound. Someone should check B's exhibit radius against the C.6 window before B is claimed as novel.
- Remark 6.14 is unchanged in rev 2: no attack reaching eps_mca when eps_mca > eps_ca is known. Our eps_mca-vs-eps_ca lanes remain unclaimed.

FRONTIER MOVERS (not scoops of the 23, but read next)
- ePrint 2026/1432 (Jo, 2026-07-13, post-v3), abstract accessed=yes, verbatim: "As a concrete application to the Grand MCA Challenge, we exhibit a single prime field F_Q, with Q<2^256, that supports the required smooth domains at all four target rates. With K=2^18, the first post-Johnson budget has MCA error below 2^-128 at rates 1/2,1/4,1/8, and 1/16, as does the second such budget at rate 1/8." This is MCA-side, deterministic upper bounds at O(1/n) past Johnson (delta ~ 0.293 at rate 1/2), so it does NOT reach target 2's near-capacity band at delta ~ 0.4961; but it is a live claim of progress on grand challenge 1 and its "largest safe integer budget / next one unsafe" framing is the same adjacent-crossing shape as headliner F on the eps_mca side. Highest-priority full read.
- ePrint 2026/782 (KKH), abstract accessed=yes: proof uses "a new additive-combinatorics lemma on sums of roots of unity", and ABF cite stronger low-q versions of Lemma C.2 while stating they "do not apply" to their own Section 6.4 codes. This single document is the pivot for targets 5, 7, 9, 10, 11 and for the WCL slots: if its low-q lemma reaches q < 2^256 at deployed s, generator_economy gets a near-free construction and headliner C's slot decomposition comes under pressure; if it contains a growing-order norm bound, f2_growing_order_myerson is either solved or scooped. Full read is the top follow-up.
- arXiv 2604.09724 (Kambire) and arXiv 2607.08516 (Goyal-Guruswami-Sun-Wootters): not re-verified this session (accessed=no); the digest grades them WATCH and LOW RISK respectively.

LEDGER CORRECTIONS TO APPLY (from the digest, both consequential)
1. [Jo26] in ABF Thm 4.7 (eps_mca(C^{==t}, delta) = eps_mca(C, delta)) = ePrint 2026/891 ("Interleaving Stability for MCA and Curve Decodability", rec. 2026-05-06), NOT 2026/1432. Fix provenance in all m_handling consumers.
2. rev-2 Definition 2.12 is COSET-FORM: "a multiplicative coset of a subgroup H subset F* whose order is a power of two". Our coset analysis is now the exact official object, not a conservative superset; the intro prose still says "multiplicative subgroup" twice, so cite the definition verbatim and keep the subgroup case as the theta = 1 specialization.

mappings.argument: ABF rev-2 Appendix C (Cor. C.6/C.7, restating [KKH26] = ePrint 2026/782) is the only new engine producing 'many codewords at one agreement' on smooth domains - literally the shape needed to refute the B*=3 obstruction at agreement 3n/4 - and it demonstrably cannot reach that point at our row. Their construction fixes the word x^{rm} on L with n=m*s, psi(x)=x^m onto G (|G|=s), and returns tails u_S of r-subsets S; agreement is exactly rm and deg u_S <= (r-q-1)m < k where q is the number of elementary symmetric functions pinned across the family (q=0 in C.6, q=1 in C.7 antipodal). At n=2^41, k=2^40, agreement 3n/4 forces r=3s/4 and q >= s/4 = |G\S|; since Prod_S(Y)*Prod_{G\S}(Y) = Y^s-1, pinning e_1..e_{s/4}(S) determines Prod_{G\S} completely, so EVERY admissible useful family is a singleton - one codeword, never 4 > B*=3. The boundary escape (zero-sum r-subsets when (r-1)m=k, i.e. s=4, r=3) is empty because no 3-subset of mu_4 sums to zero. Their agreements are multiples of m, so agreement 3n/4-1 is unreachable in principle. The digest's own verdict ('explicitly NOT touched') is confirmed and upgraded to a proof of non-borrowability. accessed=yes (pinned rev-2 PDF sha256 426a979c...).
mappings.what_would_be_needed: Cannot transport: would require a non-singleton family with q >= s/4 pinned symmetric functions, which the identity Prod_S*Prod_{G\S}=Y^s-1 forbids. Re-grade only if a future KKH variant produces codewords at agreements that are NOT multiples of m, or if ePrint 2026/782's full text contains a low-weight vanishing-sum classification usable at agreement 3n/4-1. Separately, Jo ePrint 2026/1432 does adjacent safe/unsafe budget determinations but on eps_mca, not on L_1, so it is not an input here.

mappings.argument: Overlap named: HEADLINER A (cyclic quotient-rotation list floor at rate 1/2, c=2^33 specialization), which is the theorem that retired the list half of this node. ABF Appendix C Cor. C.6 and C.7 publish UNCONDITIONAL worst-case list lower bounds at every smooth rate-1/2 row (no field-size hypothesis), credited to [KKH26] = ePrint 2026/782 (rec. 2026-04-20) and slightly generalized by ABF (rev 2, July 2, 2026) - the same species of result. Quantified non-overlap, re-derived here: at official rows k and m=n/s are powers of two, so the windows (r-1)m < k <= rm (C.6) and (r-2)m < k <= rm (C.7) force sigma := a-k in {0,m}, i.e. sigma is 0 or a power of two. At the razor row (n=2^41, k=2^40) the band (2^33, sigma*=8,592,912,738] contains no power of two, so ABF reach nothing in its interior; their best razor-row point is s=256, r=129, sigma=2^33 (our already-covered endpoint) with |Lambda| >= binom(127,64)=2^123.17, which beats B*=q/2^128 only for q < 2^251.17 - void at the cap. Our floor reaches sigma_0 = 8,594,128,895 > sigma* at all q < 2^256. I also reproduced their Table-5 headline exactly as s=128, r=65, m=2^14, sigma=2^14 at KoalaBear q=p^6=2^185.93: binom(63,32)=2^59.67 > B*=2^57.93, list/q = 2^-126.26 vs their reported 2^-125.14 - confirming the mechanism and confirming it is a q~2^186 phenomenon, NOT a general official-row ceiling as the digest's relevance note suggested. Finally, this node's true residual (support-wise MCA/CA crossing, trigger ~ q/k) is untouched: Remark 6.14 states no eps_mca-reaching attack is known.
mappings.what_would_be_needed: (1) Prior-art citation of ABF App. C + KKH26 in headliner A's writeup, with an explicit strict-improvement paragraph (non-power-of-two sigma up to sigma_0, validity to q=2^256 where binom(127,64) fails, constant common-support arities). (2) Re-run the C.7 instantiation at each deployed row - especially KoalaBear n=2^21, q=2^185.93 where their sigma=2^14 point IS live - to confirm it lies inside our covered region and not inside a KoalaBear-specific band. (3) Correct the digest's claim that delta*=0.492 pins the official-row band ceiling: at the razor row that delta corresponds to sigma=2^34, twice sigma*, and the supporting binomial (2^60.2) is far below B*. Nothing here moves the MCA/CA residual.

mappings.argument: Lemma C.2 [KKH26, Lemma 1] as restated by ABF is an anti-concentration statement of exactly the P-B shape: a lower bound |Lambda_F| >= 2^r * binom(s/2, r) on the number of DISTINCT values taken by structured sums over a power-of-two-order multiplicative subgroup of a prime field (spread, not concentration). The transport fails on both objects and hypotheses: their variables are subset sums of roots of unity, not post-strip live slopes at low core, and the only separation device is the brute height bound q > s^{s/2} (2^448 already at s=2^7), which is the opposite of a fine spread estimate and is unavailable at our caps. No inequality in ABF can be instantiated on slopes.
mappings.what_would_be_needed: Would need the underlying technique, not the statement: ePrint 2026/782's 'new additive-combinatorics lemma on sums of roots of unity' (abstract accessed=yes, full text accessed=no) read and re-derived for slope differences at low core. Only a genuinely low-q spread lemma there could raise this to ADAPT.

mappings.argument: KKH's hypothesis q > s^{s/2} in Lemma C.2 exists solely to stop distinct characteristic-0 subset sums of s-th roots of unity from colliding modulo p - i.e. it is the crude surrogate for precisely the Myerson-type norm lower bound at growing 2-power order that F2 targets. So our F2 lane is the missing ingredient in their own hypothesis, not the other way round. ABF themselves state verbatim: 'Stronger versions of the above lemma are known (in particular with weaker requirements on q, see [KKH26]), but to our understanding they do not apply to the Reed-Solomon codes in Section 6.4.' ABF contains no norm bound, no Gaussian periods, no Frobenius-tower/moving-sector structure, so nothing is transportable as stated.
mappings.what_would_be_needed: Full read of ePrint 2026/782 (accessed=no; abstract accessed=yes, advertises 'a new additive-combinatorics lemma on sums of roots of unity'). If their low-q lemma is powered by a growing-order norm/Gaussian-period lower bound, F2 re-grades immediately to DIRECT_USE or, if their bound covers our regime, to SCOOP_RISK on the F2 lane. This is the single highest-value follow-up read in the whole cross-reference.

mappings.argument: A norm gate - a p-specific multiplicative coincidence in which a bounded-height cyclotomic integer vanishes mod p - is exactly the event KKH's q > s^{s/2} hypothesis excludes wholesale rather than counts. ABF's restatement therefore contains the right failure mode but with the opposite treatment: an all-or-nothing field-size exclusion, no per-prime analysis, no h >= 4 structure, and no counting statement of any kind. At official rows (q < 2^256) the hypothesis is unavailable, so their route is silent on how often the gate opens.
mappings.what_would_be_needed: A low-q variant that PRICES individual coincidences instead of excluding all of them; ePrint 2026/782's full text is the only place such a statement could live. Re-grade to ADAPT only if that paper bounds the number of vanishing events rather than assuming none.

mappings.argument: ABF's Cor. C.7 antipodal families are built from primitive 2-null blocks: for s even, alpha in G iff -alpha in G, and each pair has sum 0, which is what pins lambda_1 across the family (the r-odd branch keeps one unpaired element). That is exactly the t=2 case of the primitive t-null blocks u2 must decide, and Def. C.3's ((G,r,q)-useful families with pinned lambda_1..lambda_q) shows that larger null blocks are precisely the fuel needed for q >= 2 pinning. But ABF need only the existence of one structured family: there is no decision procedure, no per-row statement, no block-size bound b <= C log n, and no certificate format. The direction of use is also inverted - they want null structure to exist, we must certify existence/nonexistence per row.
mappings.what_would_be_needed: A statement bounding or enumerating the primitive null blocks of mu_s at prescribed order (nothing of the kind is in ABF). Re-grade to ADAPT if ePrint 2026/782's additive-combinatorics lemma classifies short vanishing sums of 2-power-order roots of unity, since that classification is the mathematical core of the u2 certifier.

mappings.argument: Lemma C.2 [KKH26, Lemma 1] is our exact primitive: from a power-of-two-order multiplicative subgroup G of a prime field it produces |Lambda_F| >= 2^r * binom(s/2, r) pairwise-distinct subset-sum values, built from r-subsets of half the antipodal pairs - i.e. half-size subset-sum centers over a 2-power subgroup. The magnitude is adequate for our demand: at s=128, max_r 2^r*binom(64,r) = 2^98.19 >= B*/2^33 <= 2^95 (and at deployed s = 2^21 the count is astronomically larger). Two real gaps stop it being DIRECT_USE. (a) The hypothesis q > s^{s/2} is 2^448 at s=2^7 and 2^22020096 at s=2^21, violating q < 2^256 by orders of magnitude; ABF explicitly note stronger low-q versions exist in [KKH26] but that 'to our understanding they do not apply' even to their own Section 6.4 codes. (b) C.2 counts distinct VALUES only; generator_economy additionally requires the pairwise differences to lie in height-budget units times a poly(N')-generated multiplicative semigroup, and requires an e_1-distinctness guard against counting collisions as distinct centers - neither is present.
mappings.what_would_be_needed: (1) Full read of ePrint 2026/782 (accessed=no) to extract the low-q variant and its exact q-threshold at deployed s; if it reaches q < 2^256 the counting half of this node is essentially handed to us (and simultaneously becomes competitive pressure on our construction). (2) Prove the difference structure ourselves on top of C.2's family: differences of its centers are signed sums of roots of unity, so the semigroup/height-budget claim must come from our own zeta^a - zeta^b = zeta^b(zeta^{a-b}-1) germ, which C.2 does not supply. (3) Add the e_1 non-collision guard, absent from C.2. If (1) fails to reach q < 2^256, this mapping downgrades to ANALOGY_ONLY.

mappings.argument: Definition C.3 ((G,r,q)-useful families with pinned lambda_1..lambda_q) and Claim C.4 are the constructive dual of this target: they exhibit families whose prescribed elementary-symmetric cancellations hold, whereas we must certify that NO ternary (0,+-1) kernel vector of weight <= 2l' exists in an explicit cyclotomic-relation integer lattice at a knife-edge row. Their conditions are structural and unconditional in q (antipodal pairing, symmetric-function pinning), never exhaustive over a row, and carry no proof-logging or machine-checkable output - the opposite end of the certificate/search axis from the VeriPB-style artifact this node needs.
mappings.what_would_be_needed: Cannot transport as a certificate: an existence criterion for structured relations is not a nonexistence proof for all bounded-weight relations. Usable only as a cheap pre-filter - any knife-edge row admitting a (G,r,q)-useful family is automatically NOT certifiable - which is worth one pass before the bake-off. Re-grade if 2026/782 contains an exhaustive classification of low-weight relations at 2-power order.

mappings.argument: rev-2 Definition 2.12 is now coset-form verbatim: 'We say that a set L subset F is smooth if it is a multiplicative coset of a subgroup H subset F* whose order is a power of two.' This is directly load-bearing for c2pp, whose whole content is routing quotient/coset classes in the nested tower and pricing noncoset accidents: the official evaluation domain is now a coset D = theta*H by definition, so coset-class routing is mandatory scope rather than a conservative superset we chose, and noncoset accidents are in-scope objects that the joint reserve must price. The caveat is documented in the digest: the paper's introductory prose still calls L a 'multiplicative subgroup' twice, an internal inconsistency in rev 2. accessed=yes (pinned rev-2 PDF sha256 426a979c...); the v3 (2026-07-06) text is accessed=no, so the definition is verified only through July 2.
mappings.what_would_be_needed: (1) Re-audit the c2pp routing to confirm every clause is stated for an arbitrary coset representative theta and not implicitly for theta = 1; any step that used H-closure (x,y in D implies xy in D) must be re-derived for D = theta*H, where products land in theta^2*H. (2) Cite Def. 2.12 verbatim plus one defensive line noting the subgroup reading is the theta = 1 specialization, so the argument covers both readings of the paper. (3) Re-hash and re-check Def. 2.12 against v3 when Cloudflare clears.

mappings.argument: ABF's only cancellation mechanism on smooth subgroups is the antipodal 2-null block (s even, alpha in G iff -alpha in G, common sum 0), used in Cor. C.7 with the odd branch |Lambda| >= binom(s/2-1,(r-1)/2) obtained by fixing one unpaired element. Our window has already quotiented that mechanism out: zeta of exact order 512 satisfies zeta^256 = -1, so every antipodal cancellation pairs exponents differing by 256, and the prescribed support window [0,256) contains no such pair. Hence ABF's engine contributes zero candidate weight-5 vanishers - consistent with emptiness, but no evidence for it. Structurally, their odd-r branch has no mechanism for the unpaired element beyond fixing a single one, which is exactly the parity residue this odd-weight slot is about; and all their statements are LOWER bounds on family/list size, never emptiness at a prescribed exact order.
mappings.what_would_be_needed: Nothing in ABF bounds signed weight-w vanishing sums at exact order. The live external item is ePrint 2026/782's 'new additive-combinatorics lemma on sums of roots of unity' (abstract accessed=yes, full text accessed=no): read it and check whether it classifies low-weight vanishers at 2-power order - that could either supply this slot's proof (re-grade DIRECT_USE/ADAPT) or put headliner C's ten-slot decomposition under scoop pressure.

mappings.argument: Even-weight slot. Cor. C.7's even-r branch |Lambda| >= binom(s/2, r/2) is built entirely from r/2 antipodal pairs - i.e. from exactly the trivial signed vanishers that our support window already excludes: zeta has exact order 512 so zeta^256 = -1, and no two exponents in [0,256) differ by 256. ABF therefore exhibit precisely the cancellation family our normalization removes, and say nothing about the residual weight-6 vanishers over the window. Their statements are also lower bounds on family size, never emptiness, and are never made at a prescribed exact order over admissible primes (v_2(q-1) >= 41, q < 2^256).
mappings.what_would_be_needed: Cannot transport: an existence construction of pair-based cancellations is orthogonal to a zero-event obligation over a pair-free window. Re-grade only on a classification result for bounded-weight vanishing signed sums at exact 2-power order, plausibly in ePrint 2026/782 (full text accessed=no).

mappings.argument: Odd-weight slot. Same core as slot (1,5): ABF/KKH's mechanism is antipodal 2-null blocks with one unpaired element in the odd branch binom(s/2-1,(r-1)/2), and the window [0,256) with zeta^256 = -1 excludes all antipodal pairings by construction, so their families produce no weight-7 vanisher candidates. Their odd-r handling is a single fixed element, with no machinery for genuinely odd cancellation patterns - which is the residue this slot must kill. No emptiness statement, no exact-order statement, no official-prime restriction anywhere in ABF.
mappings.what_would_be_needed: A classification of odd-weight signed vanishing sums at exact 2-power order; not in ABF. Read ePrint 2026/782 in full (accessed=no) to test whether their roots-of-unity lemma covers odd weights.

mappings.argument: Even-weight slot, same structure as (1,6): the even branch binom(s/2, r/2) of Cor. C.7 is a union of 4 antipodal pairs at weight 8, exactly the trivial vanishing pattern excluded by the support window [0,256) under zeta^256 = -1. ABF supply an existence construction of such patterns on smooth subgroups; our obligation is a zero-event claim after those patterns are removed. Different direction, different quantifier (their families need one q, ours must hold at every official-admissible prime with v_2(q-1) >= 41, q < 2^256).
mappings.what_would_be_needed: Cannot transport. Only a bounded-weight vanishing-sum classification at exact order 512 would help; check ePrint 2026/782's additive-combinatorics lemma (full text accessed=no).

mappings.argument: Odd-weight slot at L=2 (exact order 1024, two prescribed vanishings at zeta and zeta^3, support in [0,512)). ABF's engine is antipodal pairing at zeta^512 = -1, which the window [0,512) excludes wholesale, so their families yield no candidate weight-7 vanishers. Additionally ABF have no mechanism at all for SIMULTANEOUS vanishing at several odd powers of the same root: their pinning is of elementary symmetric functions of a subset (Def. C.3), one linear condition per pinned lambda on a single evaluation, not a multi-Galois-conjugate condition. So even the shape of the L=2 slot is outside their framework.
mappings.what_would_be_needed: A statement about signed polynomials vanishing simultaneously at several odd powers of a fixed root of exact 2-power order; absent from ABF. Only ePrint 2026/782's full text could plausibly contain a usable ingredient (accessed=no).

mappings.argument: Even-weight L=2 slot. Cor. C.7's even branch produces exactly antipodal-pair cancellations (zeta^512 = -1 at exact order 1024), which the support window [0,512) removes by construction; and ABF's pinning machinery handles one evaluation point, not simultaneous vanishing at zeta and zeta^3. Their results are family-size lower bounds, never emptiness, and hold for a chosen field rather than for every official-admissible prime.
mappings.what_would_be_needed: Cannot transport. Would need a multi-conjugate low-weight vanishing classification at exact order 1024; check ePrint 2026/782 (accessed=no).

mappings.argument: Odd-weight L=2 slot. Same two obstructions as (2,7): (i) ABF's only cancellation primitive is the antipodal 2-null block, excluded by the support window [0,512) with zeta^512 = -1; (ii) their odd branch merely fixes one unpaired element (binom(s/2-1,(r-1)/2)) and offers no account of odd-weight cancellation, and no framework for simultaneous vanishing at zeta and zeta^3. The direction is also inverted - they construct, we must certify emptiness at every official-admissible prime.
mappings.what_would_be_needed: An odd-weight, multi-conjugate vanishing classification at exact 2-power order; absent from ABF, possibly touched by ePrint 2026/782's roots-of-unity lemma (accessed=no).

mappings.argument: Odd-weight L=4 slot (exact order 2048, four odd-power vanishings, support in [0,1024)). ABF's antipodal mechanism corresponds to exponent differences of 1024 and is excluded by the window; their odd-r branch fixes a single unpaired element and provides no odd-weight theory; and nothing in Def. C.3/Cor. C.7 handles four simultaneous Galois-conjugate vanishing conditions - their pinned lambda_1..lambda_q are symmetric functions of one subset evaluated once, not conditions at several odd powers. Toolbox adjacency only (both live on signed sums of 2-power roots of unity).
mappings.what_would_be_needed: A classification of low-weight signed vanishers subject to several conjugate conditions at exact order 2048; not in ABF. Full read of ePrint 2026/782 (accessed=no) is the only external lead.

mappings.argument: Even-weight L=4 slot. Cor. C.7's even branch binom(s/2, r/2) is exactly the family of 5 antipodal pairs at weight 10, i.e. the trivial vanishers already removed by the support window [0,1024) with zeta^1024 = -1 at exact order 2048; and ABF have no framework for the four simultaneous odd-power vanishing conditions this slot imposes. Existence construction vs zero-event obligation, and per-field vs all-official-primes quantifiers.
mappings.what_would_be_needed: Cannot transport. Re-grade only on a bounded-weight multi-conjugate vanishing classification at exact order 2048; check ePrint 2026/782 (accessed=no).

mappings.argument: Odd-weight L=4 slot, the deepest of the ten. All three ABF limitations bind at once: the antipodal primitive is excluded by the support window [0,1024) (zeta^1024 = -1 at exact order 2048); the odd branch of Cor. C.7 handles odd cardinality only by fixing one element; and Def. C.3's pinning cannot express four simultaneous vanishing conditions at distinct odd powers. Four separable layers, with sharply different usefulness at prize rows:
(a) Asymptotic shortening exponent Psi_rho (SF1/SF3/SF4) plus an exponential-budget safe-frontier certificate. VACUOUS AT OUR ROWS: it needs theta = lim (1/n) log2(1+B*_n) > 0, and at n = 2^41..2^44 with B* ~ 2^38..2^43 we have theta -> 0. THE MOST IMPORTANT SINGLE FINDING FOR US (target 1)
HD2's proof (lines 1117-1132) uses only: (i) Cauchy-Schwarz on the retained-agreement degree sequence, and (ii) "two distinct codeword pairs agree coordinatewise on at most k-1 points, since at least one nonzero difference polynomial has degree less than k". Step (ii) is degree-blind in the interleaving parameter: for m-tuples, at least one component differs and its difference polynomial still has < k zeros. Hence the identical proof gives J_m(A) = floor(n(A-k+1)/(A^2-(k-1)n)) for EVERY interleaving degree m >= 1, uniformly. That degeneration is precisely why our P-B anti-concentration is needed, so the paper is best cited as evidence that the low-core zone is not reachable by his core route. The only other anti-concentration-flavoured content is the exact slope-incidence linearization (DRC2), which gives an aggregation identity rather than a spread bound, and the Proposition 'The recurrence boundary is not pointwise additive' (line 3163ff, DRC3): for E = {x,y} the boundary coordinate F(x,y) = eta_j xy - eta_{j+1}(x+y) + eta_{j+2} has mixed difference eta_j(x-x')(y-y') != 0, so it is NOT of the form c + g(x) + g(y) and a Fourier reduction to additive maps E -> sum_{t in E} g_gamma(t) 'requires a separate coordinate theorem'. mappings.argument: Real tool overlap, plus a conditional competing risk. Three components of the Gowers-cube package bear directly on image-fiber counts #ImgFib_U(k+sigma). mappings.argument: Their list mechanism (Thm 1 Item 1; §3 Remark 5, ePrint 2026/782) yields C(s,r-1) ~ 2^{s H_2(rho)} codewords, but only at radius 1-rho-Theta(1/s) — i.e. agreement ~ rho*n + m, just above k. At rate 1/2 with the largest s our field sizes admit (s<=512) that is agreement ~0.504n, whereas target 1 lives at agreement 3n/4 (radius n/4), deep inside Johnson, with single-digit budgets (B*=3 obstruction, four codewords at 3n/4-1). Their family contributes exactly zero codewords there: a degree-<k=n/2 polynomial agreeing on 3n/4 points is determined. Metadata independently re-verified against the arXiv abstract page this session (accessed=yes: title, authors, both version dates, abstract verbatim, "17 pages + a large table"). BOTTOM LINE. CDK is a characteristic-0 classification paper. It touches exactly one layer of our DAG — the char-0 nonvanishing layer of the ten dli_wcl slots and of the char-0 sublattice in integer_code_distance_cert — and that layer is (a) already PROVED internally and (b) provably insufficient to decide any slot. Net grade: one ADAPT (target 11), thirteen ANALOGY_ONLY, nine NONE, zero SCOOP_RISK.

WHY THE SLOTS DO NOT MOVE (the decisive local evidence). Our slot statements are char-q statements quantified over official-admissible primes, not char-0 statements. Two repo facts settle the grade:
(i) /home/u2470931/smooth-read-solomin/prize/background/nodes/dli_wcl_extended_six_slot_sparse_divisor_endpoints/proof.md (status PROVED), lines ~73-80, already contains the char-0 layer with a half-page self-contained induction: "A nonempty set of distinct 2^a-th roots of unity summing to zero contains an antipodal pair" — this is exactly CDK Lemma 3.1 specialized to p absent, i.e. the R_2-only conclusion. The same proof then runs Nullstellensatz to a nonzero integer Delta and concludes "the characteristic divides Delta". So CDK reproves, from outside, a step we own; it adds citability and independent confirmation, not new reach.
(ii) /home/u2470931/smooth-read-solomin/prize/critical/nodes/dli_wcl_slot_1_6_emptiness/statement.md states: "(1,6)-shaped relations EXIST at non-ambient primes (the engineered weight-6 witness) — the official-admissibility gate (v_2(q-1) >= 41) is load-bearing." Since realizations exist in some characteristics, NO characteristic-0 theorem — CDK's or anyone's — can close any slot. The entire content of all ten slots is the divisibility question "does some q < 2^256 with v_2(q-1) >= 41 divide the cyclotomic norm / the descent discriminant Delta?", on which CDK is silent (digest: zero occurrences of finite fields, characteristic p, reduction mod p, resultants, cyclotomic norms).

WEIGHT BUDGET / MARGIN (useful, and sharper than the digest). The surviving residual is exactly ell in {1,2,4} with w in (2ell, ell+7] (Newton short-window exclusion w <= 2ell kills the rest), so max slot weight is 11. That is inside Poonen–Rubinstein's 1998 classification to weight 12 already (CDK abstract, accessed=yes), so for our residual the older, more-established PR98 classification suffices on its own; CDK's extension to 16 buys 5 weights of margin and an independent recheck, and CDK Lemma 2.1 (from Mann 1965 Thm 1) gives the squarefree-relative-order fact at ALL weights, so the char-0 layer never becomes the binding constraint even if the window is extended. Height: all our ledger objects are ±1 signed-shift orbits by construction (background/nodes/dli_wcl_raw_ledger_interface_guardrail/statement.md), so CDK's height-1 theorem is a reassurance, not a needed lemma; its first failure point (height-2 minimal sorou at weight 21, CDK Conjecture 4.5(b), Table 2) sits 10 weights above our worst slot.

ODD-WEIGHT SLOTS. For (1,5),(1,7),(2,7),(2,9),(4,9),(4,11) the char-0 layer is doubly closed: any char-0 vanishing sum of 2-power relative order decomposes into R_2 antipodal pairs, hence has even weight. Again char-0 only; irrelevant mod q.

NEW LEAD FOR THE LAYER THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS (surfaced this session, not in the digest). T. Y. Lam and K. H. Leung, "On vanishing sums of m-th roots of unity in finite fields", arXiv:math/9605216 (MSRI 1996-028, 1996-05-02); accessed=yes (abstract page only — I have NOT read the body, and I do not vouch for the numbered results beyond the abstract). Per the abstract it studies exactly the missing layer: which weights n lie in the char-p weight set W_p(m) for m-th roots of unity in characteristic p, giving thresholds n_0 with all n >= n_0 admissible. Shape match to our slots (m = 512L, p = q); caution: it is an EXISTENCE/threshold result over unsigned sums, so it will not by itself produce per-prime exclusions under the v_2(q-1) >= 41 gate — but it is the correct literature thread for a follow-up deep read, together with the char-0 companion Lam–Leung, J. Algebra 224 (2000) 91-109 (the "On vanishing sums of roots of unity" thread surfaced in search, accessed=no).

0. BOTTOM LINE
============================================================
Exactly ONE actionable import in the whole digest, and it is not the mu_d-rigidity content that the three
papers are famous for: it is the SECOND-HAND Mattarei bound that Cochrane quotes as his Lemma 5.4.
Verified in-house arithmetic (below) shows it would flip the DSP8 nodal sub-lane from "barred by our own
PROVED constant barrier" to "compliant with 26% margin" — conditional on ONE named extension (subgroup ->
two-coset twist). Everything else is analogy: the Kalmynin/KYY/Cochrane theorems are exact-representation
(all-or-nothing set-equality) rigidity statements, and every one of our 23 targets is a COUNTING or
EMPTINESS-mod-q target. Set-equality rigidity cannot supply counts.

Both scoop flags raised by the digest are DOWNGRADED after checking our own files (Sections 3-4).
No headliner A-G is scooped.

============================================================
1. THE ONE ACTIONABLE IMPORT (target 6, f3_h3_dsp8_correlation_bound)
============================================================
1.1 What the external statement is, verbatim, and how I verified it.
Cochrane, arXiv:2602.04111v1, "Multiplicative Subgroups of Z_p^* that are Generalized Arithmetic
Progressions" (accessed=yes: abstract page AND full PDF text-extracted). Verbatim, from the extracted text:

  "r(c) := #{(x, y) in A_k x A_k : x + y = c}."
  "Lemma 5.4 ([8]; Corollary). If k >= 4 and t <= (1/4) k^3, then for any nonzero c we have
   r(c) <= 3 * 2^{-2/3} t^{2/3}."
  reference [8] = "S. Mattarei, On a bound of Garcia and Voloch for the number of points of a Fermat curve
   over a prime field, Finite Fields and Their Applications 13 (2007), no. 4, 773-777."

Here A_k = subgroup of k-th powers in Z_p^*, |A_k| = t, k = (p-1)/t. Cochrane derives r(c) from the Fermat
curve x^k + y^k = c z^k (his eq. (5.1) is the Hasse-Weil version; Lemma 5.4 is Mattarei's refinement for
small subgroups). Mattarei's own paper: accessed=no (FFA 13 (2007) 773-777, existence and pagination
confirmed via dblp/search; I read it only through Cochrane's quotation). Kalmynin and KYY abstracts:
accessed=yes (arXiv:2504.10202, v1 2025-04-14, v2 2025-05-28, DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2504.10202, no journal
ref; arXiv:2602.20919 "Multiplicative irreducibility of shifted multiplicative subgroups", Kim-Yip-Yoo,
v1 2026-02-24, v2 2026-03-13, abstract confirms the (G-1)\{0} product-set and A/A results). Their FULL
TEXTS: accessed=no — I did not re-derive the digest's Thm/Lemma numbering.

1.2 The exact reduction to OUR object (this is the load-bearing step, and it is ours, not theirs).
Our R(t) is defined at /home/u2470931/smooth-read-solomin/prize/dag.json (node f3_h3_mobius_excess_half)
as R(t) = #{(c,d) in A^2 : d/c = t} with A = (1-H)\{0}; the DSP8 proofs use the equivalent form
(background/nodes/f3_h3_dsp8_nodal_cube_preimage_envelope/proof.md eq. (2), and
background/nodes/f3_h3_dsp8_nodal_trace_parameter_router/proof.md eq. (3)):

    R(t) + 1 = #{z in H : 1 + t(z-1) in H} = #{(z,w) in H x H : t z - w = t - 1}.

Since n = 2^s is even, -1 in H, so H = -H. Therefore:
  * if t in H, the substitution z' = tz is a bijection of H and R(t) + 1 = |H cap (H + (t-1))| = r(t-1)
    EXACTLY, with c = t-1 nonzero (t != 1). Mattarei's bound then applies VERBATIM.
  * if t not in H, the object is |tH cap (H + t - 1)| — a TWO-COSET (twisted Fermat, a x^k + b y^k = c z^k)

This is the whole gap. It is exactly the "quantifier/regime mismatch" that forbids DIRECT_USE.

2199023255551 (s=41); k >= 4 holds and n <= k^3/4 holds (equivalently 4n^4 <= (p-1)^3, implied by p >= n^2).
For the order-3n cube-preimage branch (t = 3n) the same two hypotheses also hold at every s in [13,41].
So the hypotheses are satisfied across the entire target-6 window n^2 <= p <= 6^{n/4}, no threshold.

and any two nonconstant nonproportional affine forms, simultaneous K-membership < (51/16) m^{2/3}

So the single most valuable line in the digest is quantitatively confirmed: importing Mattarei's constant
for the R(t) fiber ALONE is enough to clear NSB4 on the p == 1 mod 3 rows (the p == 2 mod 3 rows at 552 n^2
were never the problem).

============================================================

(2) TWO EXPORTABLE WINDOW-UNIFORM TOOLS (no lower bound on tau; valid at every official row including the exponential top): Q_2(m,n;G) << tau^2 (OSV Rmk 3.5, quoting Kurlberg–Rudnick, Comm. Math. (5) KOALABEAR vs MERSENNE-31 ASYMMETRY (useful standing fact). KoalaBear: v_2(p−1) = 24 >= 21 puts H (order 2^21) inside F_p^*, and Tr_{F_{p^6}/F_p}(lambda f(h)) = g(h) preserves monomial support, so sextic-extension additive-character sums reduce EXACTLY to prime-field sums with tau = p^{21/31} = p^{0.677} > p^{1/2}: classical Weil is already nontrivial and OSV Thm 1.1 applies with eps ≈ 0.249 (sparse eta_r via Rmk 1.3). (6) NEW STRUCTURAL OBSERVATION worth banking regardless of grade: two of our object families are literally OSV Q_k objects. == HEADLINE VERDICT ==
NO SCOOP OF EITHER PRIZE PROBLEM. Both papers leave Grand MCA (equal-threshold / zero-loss above Johnson) and Grand LD at official thresholds open in the authors' own words; 861's abstract itself concedes that the general-input case rests on conjecture Q2 and that the (3k/2,2k) universal extension rests on Q1 (verified on the live abstract page, item 2 above). NONE of the four official prize rates (1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16) is closed for general adversaries: rate 1/4 is unconditional only for the 3-position-sparse class, rate 1/2 is conditional on the universal-k Substitution-Principle lift (their Q3), rate 1/8 sits at base-panel only, rate 1/16 is explicitly out of scope. The strongest unconditional object in the pair — 858's half-threshold CA (eps_ca(C, delta/2, delta) <= 1/|F| for every linear code) — is a *halved*-threshold statement and therefore does not touch the equal-threshold band our MCA lane owns.

== ANSWERS TO THE FOUR AUDIT QUESTIONS (condensed; theorem numbers digest-derived) ==
(1) Threshold halving vs the CS25/Kambire open-zone adversaries: the lock survives STRUCTURALLY, not by luck. Round 1 is RVW13's 2x2 solve on an overlap of size >= (1-delta)n: two gammas each delta/2-close force joint distance <= delta, by linearity alone, no polynomial structure. So Crites–Stewart (ePrint 2025/2046) deep-hole and Kambire (arXiv 2604.09724) near-capacity constructions can only attack the EQUAL-threshold conjecture, which 858 does not use — and which 858 separately shows is vacuous at FRI scale (bad-gamma count <= C(n,w), attained only when |F| > C(n,w)^2, impossible at n >= 2^13, |F| < 2^256). Rounds >= 2 sit at fixed threshold delta/2 < min(delta_J, (1-rho)/2), inside proved BCIKS/BCHKS territory (<= n bad challenges/round), total <= nR. Residual trust surface: the path-consistency catch lemma is a black box, and the query model is i.i.d.-with-replacement. The fixed-point-free involution is NOT hidden work — it is the explicit enabler of the exact 2:1 fiber coupling and holds automatically at every official row (2 | n so the coset contains -1; p = 1 mod n forces p = 1 mod 4). The genuinely necessary structural hypothesis is k = 2^m (odd k >= 3 has an explicit counterexample: x^k is at distance 1-rho yet folds to a codeword for every alpha) — note this is a real constraint against prize rows where k is not a power of two. NET EFFECT ON US: the band's STAKES change (deployed stacks now have a rigorous above-Johnson floor at ~2.2-2.3x queries, so the zero-loss question loses deployment urgency), the band's MATHEMATICS does not.
(2) Q1 vs our f2/f7: exact statement extracted and independently confirmed at abstract level (item 2). Q1 is qualitative non-vanishing of ONE explicit algebraic number per dyadic level on a zero-dimensional chain-ideal stratum over a class field of Q[sqrt(-83,860,066,393,667)]; target 5 is a QUANTITATIVE Gaussian-period-norm census-deviation bound at growing 2-power order. STRICTLY INCOMPARABLE — neither implies the other, and no partial result transfers as a statement. Three techniques transfer as tools (exact rational resultant norm at d=4; msolve vdim=1 emptiness certificate at d=8; dyadic chain self-similarity induction), and their two proposed routes (self-similarity induction; Chevalley–Warning modular descent over deployment primes) are candidate attacks we can either import for f2 or turn around and use to preempt Q1 with our Myerson machinery. Their class-field data (h = 1,709,193) explicitly rules out naive Davenport–Hasse/Hecke-L descent — a useful negative result for our own route selection.
(3) Lean / verification bar: raised only modestly. Independently confirmed (item 4): the abstract's "formally verified in Lean 4" covers the two CA-layer COUNTING inequalities, not FRI soundness. Genuine reusable value for us: both proved theorems are stated over arbitrary linear submodules and are domain-agnostic, so they could be imported as-is if we ever want a Lean CA core; and the missing piece in their build — a concrete multiplicative-coset RSIsomorphismWitness — is exactly the smooth-domain object our lanes own, i.e. an easy differentiator if we ever formalize. Their STATUS.md and CAVEATS.md are candid; no dishonesty to flag, only the abstract's over-broad phrasing.
(4) Action–orbit vs headliner A: see the SCOOP section.
